messages.author: 65c2e69354855323
messages.subject: Error in Analysis of Measurement Invariance: Error in Sigma.hat[[g]] : subscript out of bounds
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to run a anlysis of measurement invariance but I alway get an error massage.

ldw <- 'f =~ V1+V2+V3+V4+V5+V6+V7+V8+V9+V10+V11+V12'

fit.ldw <- sem(ldw, data = dat)

summary(fit.ldw, standardized =TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE)

measurementInvariance(fit.ldw, data = dat, group = 'semred', strict= TRUE, fit.measures = 'default')

Skript ends.

Error Message:

Error in Sigma.hat[[g]] : subscript out of bounds

Does anybody know what to do?

Thanks and best regards
Juliane

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Error in Analysis of Measurement Invariance: Error in Sigma.hat[[g]] : subscript out of bounds
parts:
this is what my model looks like: 
t1.hyp1 <- '
  level: 1
    KT1w =~ a*RF1K1 + b*RF1K2 + c*RF1K3 + d*RF1K4
    PAT1w =~ e*RF1PA1 + f*RF1PA2 + g*RF1PA3 + h*RF1PA4 + i*RF1PA5 + j*RF1PA6
    SKT1w =~ k*RF1SK1 + l*RF1SK2 + m*RF1SK3
  level: 2
    KT1b =~ a*RF1K1 + b*RF1K2 + c*RF1K3 + d*RF1K4
    PAT1b =~ e*RF1PA1 + f*RF1PA2 + g*RF1PA3 + h*RF1PA4 + i*RF1PA5 + j*RF1PA6
    SKT1b =~ k*RF1SK1 + l*RF1SK2 + m*RF1SK3'

Oh, you have multilevel data?  I'm not sure whether modification indices are available for MSEMs yet.  The multilevel features of lavaan are still being developed.

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/lavaan/NLmQDFAndQk/Lz7S3ntVBAAJ
fit.t1.hyp1 <- sem(t1.hyp1, s.change, cluster = "Vkst", estimator = "mlr", fixed.x = T, missing ="fiml")
As you can read at the link above, MSEM in lavaan will not yet work with missing data, and I'm not sure whether robust corrections are yet available for MSEMs.

lavaan keeps telling me this (but it prints fit measures anyway....): 
Warning message:
In lav_object_post_check(object) :
  lavaan WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negative

That is an unrelated issue to your errors.  As the warning indicates, it is just a warning that you have some estimated negative variances (i.e., a Heywood case). There are plenty of messages you can read on this forum about that very common occurrence.  I usually recommend people read this article:

http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/0049124112442138

bemas <- read.table("D:\\bemas.txt", header=TRUE)

english <- bemas[bemas$language == 2,]
model<- 'F1 =~ B1 + B2 + B3 + B4 + B5; F2 =~ M1 + M2 + M3 + M4 + M5; F1~~F2'

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Error in Analysis of Measurement Invariance: Error in Sigma.hat[[g]] : subscript out of bounds
parts:
everything works till this:
fit.config <- cfa(model, data = bemas, group = "language", estimator = "MLR")

Because you wrote over your original model by assigning the single-group cfa() output to an object called model.  Call it something unique, then "model" will still be the character string of model syntax when you run the multiple-group model.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
